messages.content:
A language learner (their own language: Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China)) pasted a draft they are about to post or send, with an optional note.

Note: (none)

Draft:
<<<
Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you,” Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?

Great work! Kudo attached~
>>>

Say where it will be posted (platform and kind of post), who will read it, what the writer wants to do, and target: the code of the language they are learning, the one most of the draft is written in (never their own language, even when the note or a passage is in it). platform, audience and purpose in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) (the writer reads them), whatever language the note is in, a short phrase each (at most about twelve words). The purpose says only what the draft and note show the writer doing; never add aims they do not show.
Also give site: the site or medium's short name as its users write it (a site name, or "Email"); community: where on it, as its users write it (a subreddit like r/name, a fic's title, a recipient), short; and reader: a plausible handle or name for one typical reader there, written the way that site shows names.
And title: the piece as an item on the writer's list, in the language of the draft, starting with a verb, the way writing prompts are titled (for example "Reply to the author of “Long Way Home”", "Ask r/WarriorCats why StarClan never came", "Thank Sam for the playlist"); at most about eight words, naming who or what it is for.
Reply with JSON only: {"site":"","community":"","reader":"","title":"","platform":"","audience":"","purpose":"","target":"en|es|fr|ja"}
